headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap in AutoGPT vs. a non-runnable reference list; prompt-injection and leakage are limited by B's lack of runtime, but conflict and cascading misuse remain plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read/write the filesystem and execute shell commands, so if awesome-python is used as copied content or a shared file, malicious instructions could be introduced. However, awesome-python is not runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, so the bridge is indirect and unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF the operator copies content from awesome-python into a file AutoGPT reads as instructions
IF AutoGPT is configured to treat file contents as trusted prompts
mitigations: Keep the reference list read-only and separate from AutoGPT working files
Disable any workflow that auto-prompts from local files
Review copied snippets before placing them into AutoGPT inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress, so it could expose local file contents if pointed at sensitive files. awesome-python is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it is not itself a leakage source; the pairwise risk is limited to accidental exposure through AutoGPT's own handling.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in AutoGPT's accessible filesystem
IF AutoGPT is instructed to transmit file contents to an external API
mitigations: Do not mount sensitive directories into AutoGPT
Audit outbound requests from AutoGPT for file-content payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while awesome-python is a non-runnable repository reference with no locking or coordination. If both are pointed at the same workspace, AutoGPT can overwrite or race on files that the reference material also uses, and uncertainty about hidden orchestration should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents share the same writable directory
IF AutoGPT is allowed to modify files that the operator also edits manually
mitigations: Use separate directories for AutoGPT and reference material
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate and act on outputs, and awesome-python may be used as a source of libraries or examples. If AutoGPT consumes that material without verification, it can propagate incorrect recommendations or actions; the pair lacks any documented verification or provenance controls, so the safer medium severity applies.
conditions: IF AutoGPT uses content from awesome-python as authoritative guidance
IF downstream automation is triggered from AutoGPT's unverified output
mitigations: Require human review before acting on AutoGPT outputs
Cross-check library recommendations against primary sources
Disable auto-execution of actions derived from retrieved content

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency constraint, or regulated workflow is documented for either agent. AutoGPT's profile lists no touched data classes, and awesome-python is a non-runnable documentation repository, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced for the shared workflow
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment
Add retention and residency checks to the workflow
Keep regulated data out of this pair
